May I post a preprint of my submitted manuscript on arXiv while it is under review at your journal?

 Best,
 Dr. Michael Chen
 Stanford University

 --- Email In ---
 Subject: Re: Question Regarding Preprint Policy

 Dear Dr. Chen,

 Effective January 2025

 1. Introduction

 The ACM Transactions on AI (ACM TAI) recognizes the evolving landscape of scientific publishing and the increasing importance of preprints in promoting rapid dissemination and open access to research. This policy statement outlines ACM TAI’s position on preprints, including definitions, posting guidelines, citation practices, and implications for manuscript submission and review.

 2. Definition of Preprints

 A “preprint” is defined as a scholarly manuscript authored by researchers that has not yet undergone formal peer review and has not been accepted or published by a journal. Preprints are typically made publicly available on non-commercial repositories such as arXiv.org , bioRxiv.org , or similar platforms prior to, or concurrent with, submission to a journal for consideration.

 3. Scope of Policy

 This policy applies to all manuscripts submitted to ACM Transactions on AI after January 1, 2025. It governs the posting of preprints during the editorial review process and after acceptance for publication.

 4. Posting Preprints Prior to Submission

 Authors are permitted and encouraged to post their manuscripts as preprints prior to submission to ACM TAI. Preprints should be posted on reputable non-commercial public repositories that provide persistent identifiers (e.g. , DOIs or arXiv IDs), ensure long-term access, and clearly label the status of the manuscript as “not peer-reviewed. ”

 Posting a preprint prior to submission does not affect eligibility for consideration at ACM TAI. Authors must disclose any preprint postings at the time of manuscript submission.

 5. Posting Preprints During Peer Review

 Authors may post or update preprints while their manuscript is under review at ACM TAI. The following conditions apply:

 a) The preprint must be identical or substantially similar to the version submitted to ACM TAI.
 b) The repository must clearly indicate that the manuscript is under consideration at ACM Transactions on AI.
 c) Authors must notify the editorial office of any new postings or updates during the review process.
 d) Any substantive changes made in response to reviewer comments should be updated in the preprint only after the revision has been formally submitted to ACM TAI.

 6. Posting Preprints After Acceptance

 Once a manuscript has been accepted for publication at ACM TAI, authors may update their preprint with an “accepted version. ” However, they must adhere to copyright and licensing requirements as outlined in Section 9 below. Authors are encouraged to link the preprint to the final published article using its DOI once available.

 7. Citation of Preprints in Manuscripts

 Authors may cite relevant preprints within their submissions to ACM TAI provided that:

 a) The cited preprint is publicly accessible via a recognized repository.
 b) The citation includes sufficient information for identification (author(s), title, repository name, identifier such as DOI or arXiv ID, year).
 c) The citation explicitly notes that it refers to a preprint (e.g. , “arXiv preprint”).

 Reviewers will be instructed to treat cited preprints appropriately and not penalize authors for citing work that has not yet undergone peer review.

 8. Reviewer Guidance Regarding Preprints

 ACM TAI reviewers are reminded that:

 a) The presence of a publicly posted preprint does not constitute prior publication nor grounds for rejection.
 b) Reviewers must evaluate the submitted manuscript independently of any public comments or feedback received via preprint repositories.
 c) Anonymous peer review remains intact; reviewers should not seek out author identities via preprint platforms if double-blind review is in place.

 9. Copyright and Licensing Considerations

 a) Authors retain copyright over their posted preprints unless otherwise agreed with the repository.
 b) Upon acceptance at ACM TAI, authors will be required to sign an appropriate copyright transfer agreement or license-to-publish arrangement with ACM.
 c) Posting the “accepted version” (post-peer-review but before typesetting) is allowed provided it is labeled appropriately and links back to the published article when available.
 d) Posting the final publisher-formatted PDF (“version of record”) is prohibited unless specifically permitted by ACM’s open access policies.

 10. Embargoes and Publicity

 There are no embargo restrictions on posting preprints before or during submission/review at ACM TAI. Authors may discuss their work publicly (e.g. , conferences, media interviews), but should clarify that findings are preliminary if based solely on non-peer-reviewed versions.

 11. a) The work has not been published in a peer-reviewed journal or proceedings,
 b) The content matches what is submitted,
 c) Disclosure is made at time of submission.

 If submitting work previously posted as a conference paper, please refer to ACM’s conference-journal overlap policies.

 12. Disclosure Requirements

 During submission, authors must provide:

 a) The URL/identifier of any relevant preprints,
 b) A statement confirming that no peer-reviewed publication exists,
 c) Notification of any subsequent updates during review.

 Failure to disclose relevant preprints may result in delays in processing or withdrawal from consideration.

 13. Handling Comments and Feedback on Preprints

 Authors who receive public comments or feedback via preprint servers are welcome to incorporate constructive input into revised submissions. However, revisions in response to reviewer feedback should be prioritized over public commentary during peer review.

 14. ACM TAI recognizes several benefits associated with posting preprints:

 - Accelerated dissemination of research findings
 - Increased visibility and citations
 - Opportunities for early feedback from peers
 - Establishment of priority for novel results

 However, authors should also consider potential risks:

 - Exposure of errors prior to peer review
 - Risk of being scooped if others build upon unreviewed results
 - Potential confusion between preliminary findings and final published versions

 Authors are encouraged to weigh these factors when deciding whether and when to post a preprint.

 15. Open Access Considerations

 Preprinting does not affect eligibility for open access publication at ACM TAI. Authors wishing to pursue Gold Open Access should consult ACM’s Author Rights page for details regarding Article Processing Charges (APCs), licensing options (e.g. , CC BY), and permitted sharing formats.

 16. Compliance with Funder Mandates

 Many funding agencies require public access to research outputs via repositories such as arXiv or PubMed Central. Posting a preprint generally satisfies most funder mandates regarding early dissemination but does not substitute for compliance with open access requirements post-publication unless explicitly permitted by the funder.

 17. Frequently Asked Questions

 Q: Will posting my work on arXiv prevent me from submitting it to ACM Transactions on AI? 
 A: No; posting your work on arXiv prior to or during submission does not affect eligibility for review at ACM TAI.

 Q: Can I update my arXiv preprint while my paper is under review? 
 A: Yes; you may update your preprint during peer review provided you notify the editorial office and ensure consistency between versions.

 Q: Do I need to cite my own or others’ relevant preprints? 
 A: Yes; all cited materials—including unpublished manuscripts—should be referenced appropriately in your bibliography.

 Q: May I share reviewer feedback publicly via my preprint? 
 A: No; reviewer reports are confidential unless explicit permission is granted by all parties involved.

 Q: What version can I post after acceptance? 
 A: You may post your accepted author manuscript (“post-print”) but not the final publisher-formatted PDF unless allowed by ACM’s policies.

 18. Policy Review Schedule

 This policy will be reviewed annually by the Editorial Board of ACM Transactions on AI. Updates will be communicated via the journal website and author guidelines.

 19. Contact Information

 For questions regarding this policy or its implementation, please contact:

 Editorial Office  
 ACM Transactions on AI  
 Email: acm-tai@acm.org 
 Website: https://tai.acm.org/

 20. References & Additional Resources

 - ACM Author Rights & Publishing Policies: https://authors.acm.org/
 - arXiv Submission Guidelines: https://arxiv.org/help/submit
 - Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE): https://publicationethics.org/
 - Funders’ Open Access Mandates (SHERPA/RoMEO): https://v2.sherpa.ac.uk/romeo/

Dear Editorial Board,

May I post a preprint of my submitted manuscript on arXiv while it is under review at your journal?

Best,
Dr.
Michael Chen
Stanford University

--- Email In ---
Subject: Re: Question Regarding Preprint Policy

Dear Dr.
Chen,

Yes, authors are allowed to post preprints on arXiv during the review process.
Please see the attached policy statement.

Sincerely,
Editorial Office, ACM Transactions on AI

--- Attachment ---
ACM Transactions on AI  
Preprint Policy Statement  
Effective January 2025

Introduction

The ACM Transactions on AI (ACM TAI) recognizes the evolving landscape of scientific publishing and the increasing importance of preprints in promoting rapid dissemination and open access to research.
This policy statement outlines ACM TAI’s position on preprints, including definitions, posting guidelines, citation practices, and implications for manuscript submission and review.

Definition of Preprints

A “preprint” is defined as a scholarly manuscript authored by researchers that has not yet undergone formal peer review and has not been accepted or published by a journal.
Preprints are typically made publicly available on non-commercial repositories such as arXiv.org
, bioRxiv.org
, or similar platforms prior to, or concurrent with, submission to a journal for consideration.

Scope of Policy

This policy applies to all manuscripts submitted to ACM Transactions on AI after January 1, 2025.
It governs the posting of preprints during the editorial review process and after acceptance for publication.

Posting Preprints Prior to Submission

Authors are permitted and encouraged to post their manuscripts as preprints prior to submission to ACM TAI.
Preprints should be posted on reputable non-commercial public repositories that provide persistent identifiers (e.g.
, DOIs or arXiv IDs), ensure long-term access, and clearly label the status of the manuscript as “not peer-reviewed.
”

Posting a preprint prior to submission does not affect eligibility for consideration at ACM TAI.
Authors must disclose any preprint postings at the time of manuscript submission.

Posting Preprints During Peer Review

Authors may post or update preprints while their manuscript is under review at ACM TAI.
The following conditions apply:

a) The preprint must be identical or substantially similar to the version submitted to ACM TAI.
b) The repository must clearly indicate that the manuscript is under consideration at ACM Transactions on AI.
c) Authors must notify the editorial office of any new postings or updates during the review process.
d) Any substantive changes made in response to reviewer comments should be updated in the preprint only after the revision has been formally submitted to ACM TAI.

Posting Preprints After Acceptance

Once a manuscript has been accepted for publication at ACM TAI, authors may update their preprint with an “accepted version.
” However, they must adhere to copyright and licensing requirements as outlined in Section 9 below.
Authors are encouraged to link the preprint to the final published article using its DOI once available.

Citation of Preprints in Manuscripts

Authors may cite relevant preprints within their submissions to ACM TAI provided that:

a) The cited preprint is publicly accessible via a recognized repository.
b) The citation includes sufficient information for identification (author(s), title, repository name, identifier such as DOI or arXiv ID, year).
c) The citation explicitly notes that it refers to a preprint (e.g.
, “arXiv preprint”).

Reviewers will be instructed to treat cited preprints appropriately and not penalize authors for citing work that has not yet undergone peer review.

Reviewer Guidance Regarding Preprints

ACM TAI reviewers are reminded that:

a) The presence of a publicly posted preprint does not constitute prior publication nor grounds for rejection.
b) Reviewers must evaluate the submitted manuscript independently of any public comments or feedback received via preprint repositories.
c) Anonymous peer review remains intact; reviewers should not seek out author identities via preprint platforms if double-blind review is in place.

Copyright and Licensing Considerations

a) Authors retain copyright over their posted preprints unless otherwise agreed with the repository.
b) Upon acceptance at ACM TAI, authors will be required to sign an appropriate copyright transfer agreement or license-to-publish arrangement with ACM.
c) Posting the “accepted version” (post-peer-review but before typesetting) is allowed provided it is labeled appropriately and links back to the published article when available.
d) Posting the final publisher-formatted PDF (“version of record”) is prohibited unless specifically permitted by ACM’s open access policies.

Embargoes and Publicity

There are no embargo restrictions on posting preprints before or during submission/review at ACM TAI.
Authors may discuss their work publicly (e.g.
, conferences, media interviews), but should clarify that findings are preliminary if based solely on non-peer-reviewed versions.

Conflicts with Other Policies

If authors have previously posted their work as a preprint elsewhere (including institutional repositories), this does not violate ACM TAI’s originality requirement so long as:

a) The work has not been published in a peer-reviewed journal or proceedings,
b) The content matches what is submitted,
c) Disclosure is made at time of submission.

If submitting work previously posted as a conference paper, please refer to ACM’s conference-journal overlap policies.

Disclosure Requirements

During submission, authors must provide:

a) The URL/identifier of any relevant preprints,
b) A statement confirming that no peer-reviewed publication exists,
c) Notification of any subsequent updates during review.

Failure to disclose relevant preprints may result in delays in processing or withdrawal from consideration.

Handling Comments and Feedback on Preprints

Authors who receive public comments or feedback via preprint servers are welcome to incorporate constructive input into revised submissions.
However, revisions in response to reviewer feedback should be prioritized over public commentary during peer review.

Benefits and Risks of Preprinting

ACM TAI recognizes several benefits associated with posting preprints:

- Accelerated dissemination of research findings
- Increased visibility and citations
- Opportunities for early feedback from peers
- Establishment of priority for novel results

However, authors should also consider potential risks:

- Exposure of errors prior to peer review
- Risk of being scooped if others build upon unreviewed results
- Potential confusion between preliminary findings and final published versions

Authors are encouraged to weigh these factors when deciding whether and when to post a preprint.

Open Access Considerations

Preprinting does not affect eligibility for open access publication at ACM TAI.
Authors wishing to pursue Gold Open Access should consult ACM’s Author Rights page for details regarding Article Processing Charges (APCs), licensing options (e.g.
, CC BY), and permitted sharing formats.

Compliance with Funder Mandates

Many funding agencies require public access to research outputs via repositories such as arXiv or PubMed Central.
Posting a preprint generally satisfies most funder mandates regarding early dissemination but does not substitute for compliance with open access requirements post-publication unless explicitly permitted by the funder.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will posting my work on arXiv prevent me from submitting it to ACM Transactions on AI? 
A: No; posting your work on arXiv prior to or during submission does not affect eligibility for review at ACM TAI.

Q: Can I update my arXiv preprint while my paper is under review? 
A: Yes; you may update your preprint during peer review provided you notify the editorial office and ensure consistency between versions.

Q: Do I need to cite my own or others’ relevant preprints? 
A: Yes; all cited materials—including unpublished manuscripts—should be referenced appropriately in your bibliography.

Q: May I share reviewer feedback publicly via my preprint? 
A: No; reviewer reports are confidential unless explicit permission is granted by all parties involved.

Q: What version can I post after acceptance? 
A: You may post your accepted author manuscript (“post-print”) but not the final publisher-formatted PDF unless allowed by ACM’s policies.

Policy Review Schedule

This policy will be reviewed annually by the Editorial Board of ACM Transactions on AI.
Updates will be communicated via the journal website and author guidelines.

Contact Information

For questions regarding this policy or its implementation, please contact:

Editorial Office  
ACM Transactions on AI  
Email:
acm-tai@acm.org 
Website: https://tai.acm.org/

References & Additional Resources

- arXiv Submission Guidelines: https://arxiv.org/help/submit
- Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE): https://publicationethics.org/
- Funders’ Open Access Mandates (SHERPA/RoMEO):
https://v2.sherpa.ac.uk/romeo/
